subject: Follow-up: Throughput & SLOs — Finex deployment
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexbank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finexbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Throughput & SLOs — Finex deployment

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to understand the Finex workload shape. Quick recap + our ask so we can size a recommended Dedicated config: 

Recap from the call:
- Primary use case: real-time customer support summarization + compliance re-ranking on transactions.
- SLO targets: 95th pct latency target of ~250ms for short-form summaries (streaming enabled), 99th pct SLA for critical re-ranks at ~500ms.
- Typical model: open LLM variant (approx 7B-13B) with streaming for the summary path and a non-streaming rerank path.
- Expected traffic pattern: steady-state 80 QPS across the routing mix, with peak bursts up to 600 QPS during morning batch windows and after-market events.
- Message sizes: summary requests average 1200 tokens input (incl. history) -> 300-600 generated tokens; rerank requests are shorter (avg 80 tokens) but happen in batches of up to 8 items.

From Redwood, next steps we agreed to provide:
1) A throughput-sizing sheet that maps QPS/tokens-per-request -> tokens/sec and recommended GPU pool sizing (instance types, expected concurrency, batching parameters).
2) Suggested runtime config for streaming vs non-streaming routes (KV cache, prefix caching, recommended batch windows).
3) Latency/throughput trade-offs and expected p50/p95 for each path under steady vs peak.
4) A cost delta for Dedicated reservation vs hosted routing for the projected monthly token volume.

Action items for Finex: can you confirm the following so we can finalize sizing?
- Expected percent split between streaming summaries vs non-streaming reranks during steady-state and peak (e.g., 60/40).
- Max acceptable cold-start latency for the streaming path (if using burst capacity).
- Any hard concurrency limits per customer session (e.g., max 3 concurrent streams per user).

I attached a first-pass solutioning deck and an initial throughput matrix that we can update once you confirm the split.

Thanks — will loop Marissa and Marcus to own the sizing doc.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finexbank.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:06:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Throughput & SLOs — Finex deployment

Rafael — thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Split: steady-state is roughly 70% summaries (streaming) / 30% rerank (non-streaming). Peak can go to 55% summaries / 45% rerank during market close.
- Regarding tokens: summaries generally have 1,200 input tokens and ~450 output on average; reranks are 60-120 tokens per item, typically 4 items per batch.
- Concurrency per user: max 2 concurrent streams per user, but overall concurrency could be high due to many users (we capped concurrent sessions at 5,000 in our load tests).
- Cold-start: we need p95 cold-starts < 1.5s for the streaming path; steady-state p95 target remains ~250ms.

We can share internal load test traces if helpful. For now, please use 5,000 concurrent sessions as an upper bound and model both the steady (80 QPS) and peak (600 QPS) scenarios you mentioned.

— Priya
Priya Shah
Engineering Manager, Finex Bank
priya.shah@finexbank.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finexbank.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Throughput & SLOs — Finex deployment

Priya — perfect, this is really helpful. A few quick clarifications from our sizing assumptions so expectations align: 

- Tokens/sec calc: for summaries we’ll conservatively size for output generation at 450 tokens * 80 steady QPS -> 36,000 output tokens/sec (steady). For peak 600 QPS that becomes 270,000 output tokens/sec (peak). We’ll account for input tokens and model forward costs as an additional ~35% overhead in the sizing sheet.
- Concurrency model: streaming imposes an active KV cache per session; assuming 2 concurrent streams/user and 5,000 concurrent sessions -> worst-case active concurrency = 10,000 streaming connections. We do not need 10k dedicated model inference contexts simultaneously if prefix caching can serve many requests; we will model effective concurrency and batching windows to reduce GPU kernel invocations.
- Latency targets: to meet p95 250ms for streaming, we recommend small batching windows (~10–20ms) and a lower max batch size for the streaming route. For rerank (non-streaming) we can use larger batch sizes to optimize throughput.

Deliverables by EOD tomorrow (Fri): updated throughput-matrix.csv with tokens/sec rows for steady/peak, recommended GPU pool sizes with expected p50/p95 numbers, and a short note on runtime config (batching/windowing, cache TTLs).

Is Marissa ok to own the sizing sheet delivery and Marcus to own the benchmark runs?

— Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finexbank.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexbank.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Throughput & SLOs — Finex deployment

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks — I’ll take point on the sizing sheet and Marcus will run the bench scripts once we have your load traces (if you can share via the Drive link Rafael included, that’d be ideal). Quick notes on approach: 

- We will produce two configs: (A) Steady-optimized Dedicated pool (targeting 80 QPS, low-cost GPUs, aggressive batching for reranks) and (B) Peak-burst pool (autoscale-enabled to handle 600 QPS spikes with pre-warmed instances for streaming).
- Initial recommended instance family: A mix of A100/80GB-equivalent for peak burst (high single-stream performance + large KV working set) and 4090/4080-equivalent for steady throughput to keep unit costs down. Exact SKUs and counts in the matrix.
- We’ll include a small section showing expected p50/p95 under three scenarios: steady, 3x sustained traffic, and a 10x flash-burst (short-lived).

Delivering the updated throughput-matrix.csv and a short notes PDF by EOD tomorrow. If the load traces arrive sooner we can shift to an earlier run and send preliminary numbers tonight.

Cheers —
Marissa Cole
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: finex-solutioning-deck.pdf, throughput-matrix.csv
